cards.q: What is a Global Unicast Address (GUA)?
cards.a: A GUA is the public, routable IPv6 address a host needs, equivalent to an IPv4 public address but plentiful, so NAT is optional. The prefix range is 2000::/3 (2000 through 3FFF).

cards.q: What is the structure of a Global Unicast Address?
cards.a: It is three parts: the global routing prefix assigned by the ISP (typically /48), the site-defined subnet ID in bits 49-64, and the 64-bit interface ID (EUI-64 or random/privacy-derived).

cards.q: Why is every LAN a /64 in IPv6?
cards.a: A /64 is required for SLAAC and Neighbor Discovery optimizations. A /48 site can be subdivided into 65,536 /64 subnets.

cards.q: What are the four ways a host gets a Global Unicast Address?
cards.a: SLAAC (router RA advertises a prefix and the host self-configures prefix plus interface ID), DHCPv6 (stateful server hands out address and options), DHCPv6-PD (site router delegates a prefix such as /56 to a CPE), and static manual configuration on interfaces.

cards.q: Can two IPv6 hosts on the same segment ping each other with only link-local addresses?
cards.a: Yes. A host's GUA is optional while link-local is mandatory and automatically configured, so same-segment reachability works with link-local alone; multi-hop routing, however, requires GUAs.

cards.q: What source address does ping6 use on a router?
cards.a: ping6 from a router prefers the interface's own address as the source.

cards.q: What does Cisco recommend for IPv6 GUA addressing?
cards.a: Use a tracked prefix from the ISP or DHCPv6-PD for the site, keep a /64 per VLAN with sequential subnets, and enable privacy extensions (temporary randomized interface IDs) on user hosts to prevent host tracking.

cards.q: How do you configure a static GUA on a Cisco IOS interface?
cards.a: In interface configuration mode, use ipv6 address 2001:db8:1:10::1/64.

cards.q: What command advertises a prefix for ND/SLAAC on a Cisco IOS segment?
cards.a: ipv6 nd prefix 2001:db8:1:10::/64, though Router Advertisement serving is enabled by default with ipv6 enable.

cards.q: What commands verify a Global Unicast Address on Cisco IOS?
cards.a: show ipv6 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 | include prefix and show ipv6 route 2001:db8:1:10::/64.

cards.q: Is a GUA automatically present on an IPv6 interface like link-local is?
cards.a: No. Link-local is automatically present while a GUA is not; a host with only a link-local address has no Internet path.

cards.q: How does EUI-64 derive an interface ID from a MAC address?
cards.a: EUI-64 takes the 48-bit MAC, inserts FFFE in the middle, and flips the U/L bit; for example the calculation is a favorite exam trap.

cards.q: Can you assume an interface ID is permanently EUI-64?
cards.a: No. Privacy extensions (RFC 4941) rotate the interface ID with temporary randomized values, so you should not assume EUI-64 is permanent.
